# Faaast

> Faaast is an intermittent fasting tracker for iPhone. Track your fasts, see your progress and build a routine that fits your life, with visual timers, a calendar of every fast and no account required. Free to use, no ads, optional Faaast Pro.

App Store name: "Faaast: Fasting Tracker". Platform: iPhone. Language: English.
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6818526484

## Pages

- [Faaast on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6818526484): download the app
- [Home](https://faaastapp.com/): what the app does, timer styles, features, privacy, Pro and FAQ
- [Support](https://faaastapp.com/support/): contact, restoring Pro, managing subscriptions, your data
- [Privacy policy](https://faaastapp.com/privacy/): what data the app handles and where it goes

## Guides

- [16:8 intermittent fasting, explained](https://faaastapp.com/guides/16-8-intermittent-fasting/): what 16:8 is, a sample day, what you can drink, how to start
- [What happens when you fast, hour by hour](https://faaastapp.com/guides/what-happens-when-you-fast/): the stages from 0 to 72+ hours with typical timings and cited sources (light ketosis around 18–24h; ketones cover about a quarter of brain energy by day 3.5; no autophagy timing claims)
- [A fasting app without an account](https://faaastapp.com/guides/fasting-app-without-account/): how Faaast keeps data on the iPhone, importing history from other apps

## Why fast (blog)

Short articles, each summarising one trusted source (linked at the end of the article):

- [Early time-restricted eating: does the time of day you eat matter?](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/early-time-restricted-eating/): A controlled trial tested eating within six hours, finishing before 3 p.m., and found health benefits even without weight loss. Based on Cell Metabolism.
- [How to start intermittent fasting when life is busy](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/how-to-start-intermittent-fasting/): Practical tips from dietitians and nutritionists for fitting intermittent fasting around work, family and sleep. Based on Healthline.
- [Intermittent fasting for women: hormones, timing and how to start](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/intermittent-fasting-for-women/): How fasting can affect women's hormones, who should avoid it, and a gentle way to start, timed around your cycle. Based on Cleveland Clinic.
- [Intermittent fasting and heart disease: the 91% study, explained](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/intermittent-fasting-heart-disease-study/): In 2024, a headline linked eating within eight hours to a 91% higher risk of dying from heart disease. Here's why experts were sceptical. Based on Becker's Hospital Review.
- [Does intermittent fasting help you lose weight? What a year-long trial found](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/intermittent-fasting-weight-loss/): A year-long trial compared eating within an eight-hour window to cutting calories alone. Here's what it means for intermittent fasting and weight loss. Based on Harvard Health Publishing.
- [Is intermittent fasting worth trying? Benefits, limits and how to ease in](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/is-intermittent-fasting-worth-trying/): How intermittent fasting compares with other diets, what short-term trials show, and how to start slowly with realistic expectations. Based on Harvard Health Publishing.
- [What is intermittent fasting, and how does it work?](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/what-is-intermittent-fasting/): Intermittent fasting is about when you eat, not what. Here's how it works, the most common schedules, and who shouldn't try it. Based on Johns Hopkins Medicine.
- [Why people try intermittent fasting: what a survey of 514 fasters found](https://faaastapp.com/why-fast/why-people-fast/): Weight loss, health or faith? A survey of 514 people who practise intermittent fasting shows why they started, which schedule they chose and how it went. Based on BMC Public Health.

## Who it's for

- People new to fasting (start at 12:12, build up to 16:8)
- People who don't want to create an account or see ads
- People who like tracking progress: calendar, streaks, records, weight, progress photos
- People doing longer fasts: 20:4, one meal a day (OMAD), 36 hours
- Not a medical app; not for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding, under 18, have had an eating disorder, or take blood-sugar-lowering medicine without a doctor's advice

## Facts

- Fasts: 16:8, 18:6, 20:4, OMAD, 12:12, 14:10, 36 hours, or any length.
- Free: eight timer styles to choose from (five free: hour blocks, ticks, gauge, filling disc, digital), a calendar with streaks, records (average, longest, total hours, streaks), weekly goal, weight in kg, lb or stones, monthly or weekly progress photos, Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, 62 achievements, weekly and monthly recap cards, light and dark mode, import from other fasting apps (CSV or JSON) and export.
- Faaast Pro: fasting stages with alerts, water and electrolytes, weight chart and Apple Health sync, automatic iCloud backup, three extra timer styles (Flip clock, Countdown, Departure board), a progress photo every day.
- Pro prices (euro): €39.99 a year, €5.99 a month, or €79.99 once. Other regions see local App Store prices.
- Privacy: no account or sign-up, no ads. Fasts, weight and photos stay on the iPhone, with optional backup to the user's own iCloud (Pro). Progress photos stay on the iPhone and in the optional iCloud backup, are never part of an export file, and can be locked with Face ID. This website counts visits anonymously with PostHog, without cookies.
- Not medical advice. Fasting stages are typical timings and vary from person to person.
- Contact: hi@arecon.eu
